public_rationale: The evidence establishes copyrighted-book memorization in specific models and substantial restrictions on web training data. Those findings support important parts of the concern. They do not establish that almost every LLM had used copyrighted material, because the model population and representative coverage are missing. The available exhaustion estimate concerns future limits, not proof that suitable data was already exhausted in September 2024.
limitations: Model-specific evidence cannot establish population-wide prevalence.
Copyrighted training material can be licensed; this assessment does not decide infringement.
A future exhaustion projection is not a measurement of current scarcity.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: LLMs are desperate for training data and almost all have ingested copyrighted material.

statement.excerpt: These models are also desperate for training data, to the point that almost every Large Language Model has ingested some sort of copyrighted material.

from_speaker: has ingested some sort of copyrighted material
our_interpretation: I read almost every as an overwhelming majority of LLMs existing by the post, allowing exceptions. I do not invent a numerical cutoff.
Ingested means used in model training. Copyrighted material includes licensed works; the statement does not by itself establish infringement.
Desperate is read as material pressure to obtain sufficient suitable training data, rather than literal exhaustion of all available text.
The period covers training history through the post date because has ingested refers to prior training. No lower date is supplied.
The phrase to the point that suggests an explanation, but this assessment tests the two factual observations rather than assuming that scarcity caused copyrighted-data use.
criteria.support_condition: Representative evidence across the LLM population establishes copyrighted training material in an overwhelming majority, alongside evidence of material training-data supply pressure by the post.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Representative evidence establishes a substantial share of LLMs trained without copyrighted material, or directly establishes the absence of the asserted data-supply pressure. A few exceptions do not contradict almost every.

evidence.publisher: Kent K. Chang and colleagues, arXiv
evidence.explanation: The study supplies empirical evidence of copyrighted material in particular OpenAI models. Its scope cannot establish the proportion across all LLMs, so it is context for the population claim.

evidence.explanation: This contemporaneous estimate places full use of the available text stock in the future under stated assumptions. It cautions against interpreting desperate as already having exhausted all data, while remaining compatible with current access pressure.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A representative audit of model families existing by September 16, 2024, with training provenance and a defined population, plus contemporaneous evidence of material data-supply constraints.
